title: Energy volatility could fast-track global EV adoption to 50% above base case
gist: Wood Mackenzie's 'electric shock' Horizons scenario models a convergence of policy, consumer behaviour and technology that lifts global EV adoption ~50% above the base case by 2040, cutting oil demand to 99 mb/d, shuttering ~40 refineries, and requiring $45bn of extra metals supply. China dominates while the US risks ceding its auto market absent bold EV bets.

insights.claim: Wood Mackenzie's base case already projects EVs jumping from 4% of the global fleet today to 25% by 2040, with an 'electric shock' scenario that could push adoption roughly 50% higher.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 50%-above-base EV path reprices oil, autos, utilities and critical minerals demand simultaneously.
insights.quote: Wood Mackenzie's base case already projects EVs jumping from 4% of the global fleet today to 25% by 2040.

insights.claim: Three converging forces could jolt EV sales far above base: governments boosting EV supply chain investment for oil-shock resilience, high fuel prices pushing consumers to switch, and faster-than-expected EV technology advances.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: The three levers give investors a checklist of leading indicators to monitor for acceleration.
insights.quote: governments boost EV supply chain investment to strengthen resilience to oil market shocks, high fuel prices prompt more consumers to switch to EVs and EV technologies advance faster than expected.

insights.claim: The electric shock scenario is triggered by Middle East conflict driving volatility in global oil markets, which strengthens the policy and consumer case for switching to EVs.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Geopolitical oil volatility acts as an accelerant for the energy transition, not just a near-term price spike.
insights.quote: As the Middle East conflict continues to drive volatility in global oil markets

insights.claim: Under the electric shock scenario, global oil demand could fall to 99 million barrels per day by 2040, 5 mb/d below the base case and roughly its current level.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Flat-to-declining oil demand caps long-run upstream capex returns and pressures oil-levered equities.
insights.quote: this "electric shock" scenario could see global oil demand fall to 99 million barrels per day (mb/d) by 2040, 5 mb/d below the base case and roughly its current level

insights.claim: Faster EV adoption could lead to the early closure of around 40 oil refineries worldwide.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Refinery stranding risk is a concrete second-order trade for downstream energy exposure.
insights.quote: potentially leading to the early closure of around 40 oil refineries worldwide

insights.claim: China reached 42% EV penetration of car sales in Q2 2026, up from 33% a year earlier, cementing its position as the global EV leader.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: China's penetration curve is the benchmark other markets are measured against.
insights.quote: China is the global leader in EVs, reaching 42% of Chinese car sales in Q2 2026, up from 33% just a year earlier.

insights.claim: Additional Chinese policy—gasoline consumption restrictions, full purchase tax exemptions and larger credits—could cut EV total cost of ownership by about 30%, pushing annual sales from 8.9 million in 2025 to 29.9 million by 2040.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A 30% TCO cut drives volume that anchors global battery and materials demand.
insights.quote: could cut the total cost of ownership for EVs by about 30%, pushing annual sales from 8.9 million in 2025 to 29.9 million by 2040

insights.claim: Chinese EV manufacturing capacity could grow by 50% by 2035, with cost advantages enabling aggressive expansion across the Global South.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Chinese export expansion threatens legacy automakers' market share in emerging markets.
insights.quote: Chinese EV manufacturing capacity could grow by 50% by 2035, with cost advantages enabling aggressive expansion across the Global South.

themes.theme: US at risk of falling behind

insights.claim: US passenger EV sales in the first five months of 2026 fell 33% year-over-year following the withdrawal of tax incentives, with EVs at just 3% of the fleet.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Policy withdrawal directly cut US EV demand, widening the gap versus China.
insights.quote: US passenger EV sales in the first five months of 2026 were down 33% from the same period of 2025 following the withdrawal of tax incentives, and EVs currently make up just 3% of the vehicle fleet.
insights.locator: The US: at risk of falling behind

insights.claim: Without advanced battery technologies and competitive supply chains, the US auto sector risks ceding its home market to international competitors and falling behind internationally.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Battery and supply-chain capability is the pivot for US automaker survival.
insights.quote: Without advanced battery technologies and competitive supply chains, the US auto sector risks ceding its home market to international competitors and falling behind internationally.
insights.locator: The US: at risk of falling behind

insights.claim: Under the electric shock scenario, decisive US policy support could bring EV total-cost-of-ownership parity with gasoline vehicles forward to 2031 (two years early) and leave the US EV fleet 51% larger than base case by 2040.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: TCO parity by 2031 is the inflection that unlocks mass US adoption if policy responds.
insights.quote: These measures could bring EV total cost of ownership parity with gasoline vehicles forward to 2031, two years ahead of the base case, leaving the US EV fleet 51% larger than the base case by 2040.
insights.locator: The US: at risk of falling behind

insights.claim: Europe's electric shock path assumes a 'grand bargain' trading tariff relief for Chinese investment in local manufacturing, yielding a European EV fleet 53% larger than base case by 2040 amid 60,000 auto layoffs announced in 2026.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: A tariff-for-investment bargain reshapes where European EVs and jobs land.
insights.quote: trading tariff relief for Chinese investment in local manufacturing, protecting jobs while accelerating the EV transition. The result could be a European EV fleet 53% larger than the base case by 2040.

insights.claim: An additional US$45 billion in greenfield metals supply over the next decade would be sufficient to support the accelerated EV growth under the scenario.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Sizes the investable capex gap for miners levered to EV materials.
insights.quote: an additional US$45 billion in greenfield metals supply over the next decade would be sufficient to support the accelerated EV growth projected under the scenario

insights.claim: Copper is the most critical bottleneck, needing annual mine capacity additions to rise from ~850,000 tonnes/year to ~960,000 tonnes/year through 2040, requiring roughly US$25 billion of investment.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Copper supply is the single tightest constraint on EV scaling—bullish for copper miners.
insights.quote: Annual mine capacity additions would need to rise from around 850,000 tonnes per year, the long-term average, to approximately 960,000 tonnes per year through 2040, requiring roughly US$25 billion of that additional investment.

insights.claim: If Chile, Peru and the US fail to streamline permitting and keep competitive fiscal terms, a larger share of copper growth shifts to state-backed Chinese entities, deepening Western supply-chain exposure.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Permitting speed is a geopolitical lever determining who controls future copper supply.
insights.quote: If established mining regions such as Chile, Peru and the US fail to streamline permitting and maintain competitive fiscal terms, a larger share of future growth will shift toward state-backed Chinese entities, deepening Western supply chain exposure.

insights.claim: Managed charging that shifts EV load to periods of ample supply must scale sharply—from 50% to 85% of charging in Europe by 2040, while the US sits at just 5% of sessions today.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Managed charging is the low-cost lever to absorb EV demand without destabilising grids.
insights.quote: In western Europe, 50% of EV charging is already managed in this way. Under the electric shock scenario, that proportion rises to 85% across Europe by 2040. The US, where managed charging currently accounts for just 5% of sessions, would need to follow suit

insights.claim: The world's 7 million public charging ports sit at just 15% utilisation, but the scenario would consume that slack quickly—China needing 4 million more ports (~US$200bn) and Europe an extra US$108bn for 2.7 million ports above base by 2040.
insights.speaker: Wood Mackenzie
insights.so_what: Charging buildout is a multi-hundred-billion-dollar infrastructure opportunity as slack disappears.
insights.quote: China would require an additional 4 million ports by 2040, representing roughly US$200 billion in incremental investment. Europe would need an extra US$108 billion to build 2.7 million additional ports above the base case.

themes.theme: Strategic implications and AI storage demand

insights.claim: For OECD countries, securing critical mineral supplies and technological know-how over time will deliver lasting strategic advantage.
insights.speaker: David Brown
insights.so_what: Frames minerals and battery IP as national-security-grade strategic assets, not just commodities.
insights.quote: For OECD countries, securing critical mineral supplies and technological know-how over time will deliver lasting strategic advantage.

insights.claim: Battery supply chains could be particularly important given the surge in energy storage demand from the global AI boom.
insights.speaker: David Brown
insights.so_what: AI-driven storage demand and EV batteries compete for the same supply chain—doubly bullish for batteries.
insights.quote: Battery supply chains could be particularly important in light of the surge in demand for energy storage resulting from the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom.
